# 1 Samuel Chapter 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 165v–166r | **Source Image:** 1SA_026_page_001.jpg, 1SA_026_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wasteland?"

**2** So Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

**3** And Saul encamped on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wasteland, beside the road. And David was dwelling in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.

**4** David sent out spies and confirmed that Saul had indeed arrived.

**5** Then David arose and came to the place where Saul had encamped. And David saw the place where Saul lay, with Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. Saul was lying within the encampment, and the troops were encamped around him.

**6** Then David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, "Who will go down with me into the camp to Saul?" And Abishai said, "I will go down with you."

**7** So David and Abishai came to the army by night, and there lay Saul sleeping within the encampment, with his spear thrust into the ground at his head. And Abner and the troops lay around him.

**8** Then Abishai said to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hand this day. Now let me pin him to the earth with one stroke of the spear — I will not need a second."

**9** But David said to Abishai, "Do not destroy him, for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?"

**10** And David said, "As the LORD lives, the LORD Himself will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.

**11** The LORD forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD's anointed. But now, take the spear that is at his head and the jug of water, and let us go."

**12** So David took the spear and the jug of water from beside Saul's head, and they went away. No one saw them, no one knew, and no one awoke, for they were all sleeping, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them.

**13** Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain far off — a great distance between them.

**14** And David called out to the army and to Abner son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" Then Abner answered and said, "Who are you that calls to the king?"

**15** And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who is your equal in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord.

**16** This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you deserve to die, because you did not guard your lord, the LORD's anointed. And now look — where is the king's spear, and the jug of water that was at his head?"

**17** And Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And David said, "It is my voice, my lord the king."

**18** And he said, "Why does my lord pursue his servant? For what have I done, and what evil is in my hand?

**19** Now therefore, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, let Him accept an offering. But if it is men, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'

**20** Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth far from the presence of the LORD, for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."

**21** Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will no longer do you harm, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly."

**22** And David answered and said, "Behold, the king's spear! Let one of the young men come over and take it.

**23** The LORD rewards every man for his righteousness and his faithfulness, for the LORD delivered you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out my hand against the LORD's anointed.

**24** And behold, as your life was precious in my eyes this day, so may my life be precious in the eyes of the LORD, and may He deliver me from all distress."

**25** Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David. You shall both accomplish much and surely prevail." So David went his way, and Saul returned to his place.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes
All three translators agreed substantially on the narrative framework and theological core of this chapter. There was strong consensus on:
- The Ziphites' betrayal (v. 1), Saul's mobilization (v. 2), and the camp setting (vv. 3, 5)
- David's refusal to harm the LORD's anointed (vv. 9-11) — all three preserve this theological principle
- The deep sleep from the LORD (v. 12) — all three identify the tardemah and attribute it to divine action
- David's taunt to Abner (vv. 14-16) and Saul's recognition of David's voice (v. 17)
- David's exile theology in v. 19 — all three convey the equation of exile from the land with exile from the LORD
- Saul's confession and final blessing (vv. 21, 25)

---
## Disagreement Log

**Verse 1** — EMET uses the interrogative form "Is-not David hiding-himself"; LOGOS renders "Is not David hiding himself"; PNEUMA converts to a declarative statement: "David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah." **SOPHIA** retains the interrogative form with EMET/LOGOS, as the Hebrew uses the interrogative he (halow), which is a meaningful rhetorical feature.

**Verse 2** — EMET: "three thousand man, [the]-chosen-ones of-Yisra'el"; LOGOS: "three thousand chosen men of Israel"; PNEUMA: "three thousand of Israel's best soldiers." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("three thousand chosen men of Israel") as it is formally accurate without the interpretive expansion to "best soldiers."

**Verse 4** — EMET: "he-knew that Sha'ul had-come to [a]-certainty"; LOGOS: "learned that Saul had come to a certain place"; PNEUMA: "confirmed that Saul had arrived." **SOPHIA** uses "confirmed that Saul had indeed arrived," blending PNEUMA's clarity with the emphatic sense of the Hebrew el-nakhon.

**Verse 5** — EMET: "the-people [were]-encamping around-him"; LOGOS: "the people were encamped around him"; PNEUMA: "his troops around him." **SOPHIA** uses "the troops were encamped around him," combining PNEUMA's more specific "troops" with the formal phrasing of LOGOS.

**Verse 7** — EMET: "And-came David and-Avishai to the-people [by]-night"; LOGOS: "So David and Abishai went to the army by night"; PNEUMA: "David and Abishai crept into the camp at night." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("came to the army by night") as the Hebrew does not specify "crept," though PNEUMA's dramatization captures the narrative tension.

**Verse 8** — EMET: "Has-delivered-up God today your-enemy in-your-hand"; LOGOS: "God has delivered your enemy into your hand this day"; PNEUMA: "God has delivered your enemy into your hands tonight." EMET: "and-into-the-ground one-stroke, and-I-will-not-repeat to-him"; LOGOS: "I will not need to strike him twice"; PNEUMA: "I won't need a second." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS for the first clause and adopts the combined phrasing "I will not need a second" from PNEUMA, rendered more formally as "I will not need to strike him twice" is also acceptable. SOPHIA selects: "let me pin him to the earth with one stroke of the spear — I will not need a second."

**Verse 9** — EMET: "Do-not-destroy him"; LOGOS: "Do not destroy him"; PNEUMA: "Don't kill him." **SOPHIA** retains "Do not destroy him" with EMET/LOGOS, as the Hebrew tashhitehu (from shahhat) means "destroy" rather than simply "kill."

**Verse 10** — EMET: "or into-battle he-will-go-down and-he-will-be-swept-away"; LOGOS: "or he will go down into battle and be swept away"; PNEUMA: "or he'll fall in battle." **SOPHIA** follows EMET/LOGOS retaining "be swept away" (Nif'al of safah) rather than PNEUMA's simplified "fall."

**Verse 12** — EMET: "a-deep-sleep of-YHWH had-fallen upon-them"; LOGOS: "a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them"; PNEUMA: "the LORD had put them all into a deep sleep." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS's phrasing, which preserves the construct relationship while being naturally readable.

**Verse 14** — EMET: "And-called-out David to the-people"; LOGOS: "David called out to the army"; PNEUMA: "He shouted to the troops." **SOPHIA** uses "David called out to the army" with LOGOS as the best formal rendering.

**Verse 15** — EMET: "Are-not you a-man?"; LOGOS: "Are you not a man?"; PNEUMA: "You're supposed to be a great warrior, aren't you?" **SOPHIA** follows EMET/LOGOS with the literal question "Are you not a man?" as the Hebrew is a straightforward rhetorical question.

**Verse 16** — EMET: "sons of-death [are] you"; LOGOS: "you deserve to die"; PNEUMA: "you all deserve to die." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("you deserve to die"), which captures the Hebrew idiom bene-mawet idiomatically without the literalism of EMET or the expansion of PNEUMA.

**Verse 19** — EMET: "let-Him-smell an-offering"; LOGOS: "let Him accept an offering"; PNEUMA: "may He accept an offering from me." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("let Him accept an offering"), which conveys the sense of the Hif'il of ruach without the overly literal "smell."

**Verse 20** — EMET: "let-not-fall my-blood to-the-ground away-from [the]-face of-YHWH"; LOGOS: "let not my blood fall to the earth far from the presence of the LORD"; PNEUMA: "Don't let my blood be spilled far from the LORD's presence." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS for formal precision.

**Verse 21** — EMET: "I-have-been-foolish, and-I-have-erred exceedingly greatly"; LOGOS: "I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly"; PNEUMA: "I have been a fool — I have made a terrible mistake." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("I have acted foolishly and have erred exceedingly") as a strong formal rendering.

**Verse 23** — EMET: "And-YHWH will-return to-each-man his-righteousness and-his-faithfulness"; LOGOS: "The LORD rewards every man for his righteousness and his faithfulness"; PNEUMA: "The LORD repays everyone for their righteousness and faithfulness." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("The LORD rewards every man for his righteousness and his faithfulness").

**Verse 24** — EMET: "may-be-great my-life in-[the]-eyes of-YHWH, and-may-He-deliver-me from-all distress"; LOGOS: "may my life be precious in the eyes of the LORD, and may He deliver me from all distress"; PNEUMA: "may the LORD value my life and rescue me from every danger." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS's rendering, which maintains the parallel structure with "precious" matching v. 21.

**Verse 25** — EMET: "Both doing you-will-do, and-also prevailing you-will-prevail"; LOGOS: "You shall both accomplish much and surely prevail"; PNEUMA: "You will do great things and will surely triumph." **SOPHIA** follows LOGOS ("You shall both accomplish much and surely prevail"), which captures the doubled infinitive absolute construction with formal dignity.
